cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 153 on-track passes, 51 pit stops, 3 cars that never finished and 2 safety cars.

cards.title: 51 places changed hands before the first lap was done
cards.text: Twenty cars funnelling into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks. Ocon, Sainz and Gasly came out of it best, and none of them had to pass anybody cleanly to do it: on lap 1 the places are simply there for whoever is brave into the first braking zone. Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the afternoon.

cards.title: 30 yellow flag calls
cards.text: Debris, spins and cars parked where they should not be. A yellow means lift and do not overtake, so it costs real lap time to whoever happens to arrive at that corner while it is out, and nothing at all to the car half a lap ahead. Most of them were waved in the same part of the circuit, around marshalling post 15, which usually means one corner kept catching people out.

cards.title: 16 overtakes on this lap alone
cards.text: Bortoleto, Hulkenberg and Colapinto all found a way through on the same lap, which almost never happens by coincidence. Cold tyres, full tanks and everybody still finding out where they belong. 8 different drivers gained a place here.

cards.title: Colapinto starts P19. Where does he finish?
cards.text: He is in a car that belongs further up the road than this, and he has the whole afternoon to prove it.
cards.reveal: P19 to P9, 10 places, and almost none of it on television. This is the drive nobody will talk about on Monday.

cards.title: 17 incidents looked at
cards.text: Turn 6 Incident Involving Cars 23 (Alb) And 87 (Bea) Noted (15:04:34). Being noted is not the same as being punished: most of these are looked at, argued over on the radio, and quietly dropped a few laps later.

cards.title: 11 penalty calls
cards.text: Albon 10s for an incident, Hamilton 5s for false start - moving before signal, Stroll 5s for track limits. A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left to serve it at, which is how a result gets rewritten twenty minutes after the flag.

cards.title: 23 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track. Put a wheel beyond it and the lap simply stops counting, however quick it was. Stroll lost 7 of them, more than anybody, which is the sort of thing that turns into a penalty if it keeps happening. It sounds pedantic until you remember the alternative is letting everybody find their own edge of the circuit.

cards.title: Track at 44°C, and falling to 38°C
cards.text: Hot tarmac punishes tyres and rewards whoever is gentlest with them. As it cools, the picture flips. It stayed dry.

cards.title: Bearman: 15 overtakes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in a Haas F1 Team, and he started P13 and finished P12. Passing is the part of this sport that looks like the whole sport on television and turns out to be the rarest thing in it: most positions change in the pit lane, not on the road.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It almost always lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it, and it is worth a point to whoever finishes in the top ten.
cards.reveal: Antonelli on lap 37, 1:31.777, in a Mercedes.

cards.title: 12 overtakes on this lap alone
cards.text: Piastri, Bearman and Sainz all found a way through on the same lap, which almost never happens by coincidence. Cars were rejoining on new rubber alongside cars that had been out there for twenty laps, and that is a free pass rather than a move. 6 different drivers gained a place here.

cards.title: Hamilton hit 351 km/h
cards.text: Top speed says as much about wing level and about sitting in somebody's tow as it does about the engine, which is why the quickest car through the trap is so rarely the quickest car over a lap. Hamilton was running a Ferrari that clearly gave something up in the corners to get it.

cards.title: Antonelli takes the lead from Leclerc
cards.text: The lead changed hands 2 times on track today, which is rarer than it sounds.

cards.title: Alonso spent the race in somebody's mirrors
cards.text: Close enough for DRS for long stretches and still no way through. This is what modern F1 traffic actually looks like, and it happened to 6 drivers today.

cards.title: 110 blue flags waved
cards.text: That is how often a backmarker had to move aside. Lapped traffic decides more races than anybody admits.

cards.title: 9 overtakes on this lap alone
cards.text: Russell, Verstappen and Hamilton all found a way through on the same lap, which almost never happens by coincidence. Cars were rejoining on new rubber alongside cars that had been out there for twenty laps, and that is a free pass rather than a move. 7 different drivers gained a place here.

cards.title: 51 stops, and the busiest lap saw 8 of them
cards.text: Once one car blinks the rest have to answer. The window opened around here and the busiest single lap was 47, with 8 cars in on the same tour. The quickest trip belonged to Russell at 28.3s, and the slowest to Stroll at 46.2s. That gap is a whole position, sometimes two, decided by people who never touch the steering wheel.

cards.title: Antonelli nursed one set for 34 laps
cards.text: On the mediums, from lap 1 to lap 35. Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane, and every lap you stretch is also a set of tyres getting slower underneath you. The whole afternoon is that argument, run at 300 km/h.

cards.kicker: Your call on the pit wall
cards.title: You are Hamilton, 0.7s behind Verstappen and going nowhere. Now what?
cards.text: Stuck in dirty air your tyres cook and your car will not turn. Stopping first gives you clean track for two or three laps, which is the whole trick behind the undercut.

choices.label: Box now and undercut
choices.sub: Fresh tyres, clean air, two laps to make it pay

choices.label: Stay out and overcut
choices.sub: Let him stop first, then push on an empty track

choices.label: Forget strategy, pass him
choices.sub: Send it and take the risk

outcomes.box: You lose about 30s in the lane and come out in traffic, betting that two fast laps on new tyres are worth more than the place you just gave up.
outcomes.wait: You stay on old rubber while he gets new ones, and you need clean air plus a mistake from him to make it work.
outcomes.attack: Passing a car with the same tyres on the same fuel is the hardest thing in the sport, and running into the back of him ends both afternoons.

cards.reveal: Hamilton came in on lap 48, 13 laps after this. He finished P3, Verstappen P20.

cards.title: Leclerc had the quickest car underneath him
cards.text: Ranked on median clean lap, which strips out traffic, safety cars and one-off heroics. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Lap 36: contact between Russell and Verstappen at Turn 15. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and the whole thing lands on your desk while the cars keep circulating. Same call the stewards had to make, same three seconds to think about it.

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the afternoon on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if they never stop again. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards went with no action.

cards.title: Hulkenberg is out
cards.text: The Audi stops after 37 of 52 laps, running P15 at the time from P12 on the grid. He had made 13 passes getting there. Teams almost never say what broke on the day, and the timing feed only records that he stopped. Zero points weekends are where title fights quietly bleed.

cards.title: Antonelli: 1:31.777
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all afternoon, in a Mercedes, and it came on lap 37 of 52. They almost always do: by then the fuel is nearly gone, the car is at its lightest of the day, and the track has an afternoon of rubber laid into it. A lap 1 time and a lap 50 time are barely the same sport.

cards.title: Albon stopped 5 times
cards.text: Three stops when the field is doing one or two means something went wrong, or somebody gambled.

cards.title: One of these three does not see the chequered flag. Who?
cards.text: Nothing on the timing screens says it is coming. That is rather the point of mechanical failure.
cards.reveal: Verstappen, on lap 47 of 52, the Red Bull Racing car stopping without warning.

cards.title: Albon is out
cards.text: The Williams stops after 44 of 52 laps, running P21 at the time from P16 on the grid. He had made 1 passes getting there. Teams almost never say what broke on the day, and the timing feed only records that he stopped. Zero points weekends are where title fights quietly bleed.

cards.title: Antonelli went the other way: 14 places lost
cards.text: P1 on the grid, P15 at the flag, and 3 stops when most of the field did 2. Strategy, damage, or simply a car that would not do on Sunday what it did on Saturday. Qualifying flatters whoever can put one lap together; a race asks for sixty.

cards.title: Verstappen is out
cards.text: The Red Bull Racing stops after 47 of 52 laps, running P3 at the time from P7 on the grid. He had made 10 passes getting there. Teams almost never say what broke on the day, and the timing feed only records that he stopped. Zero points weekends are where title fights quietly bleed.

cards.title: Verstappen was running P3 when the car gave up. Where does he finish if it holds together?
cards.text: Nobody can answer this one for certain, which is exactly why it is still being argued about. You have his own lap times to go on and nothing else.

choices.label: Podium, not the win
choices.sub: Close, but the leader had it covered

choices.label: Swallowed by the pack
choices.sub: Traffic and tyres get him anyway

outcomes.win: For this to happen he needs the leader to have nothing left, and leaders rarely do.
outcomes.podium: The safe read, and the boring one. Track position plus his pace usually lands you here.
outcomes.midfield: It takes one bad restart or one long stint to fall through the field, and it happens more than people think.

cards.reveal: Our read from his own lap times, not a fact. He was lapping 0.18s a lap slower than Leclerc, who went on to win it, and he was ahead of 4 of the five drivers who ended up at the front. Take 47 laps of that and P3 is the honest guess. The car had other ideas and nobody gets to check.

cards.title: Every gap on track, erased
cards.text: Leclerc was leading when it came out and dived straight in, along with Hadjar, Lawson, Lindblad and 9 others. Neutralised until lap 51. Every gap on track was wiped, so a lead built over twenty laps was worth nothing at the restart, and whoever had fresher tyres underneath him suddenly had a race again.

cards.title: Colapinto: P19 on the grid, P9 at the flag
cards.text: 10 places gained, 6 of them by passing somebody on track. This is the drive nobody will mention on Monday, because the cameras live at the front and the story of a race is written from there. The timing sheet does not care where the cameras were.

cards.kicker: Your call on the pit wall
cards.title: Safety car with 4 laps left. You are leading. Box or stay out?
cards.text: The pack is bunched up behind you and a stop costs you far less than usual, except that everybody behind can copy you and the one who does not gets the lead.
state: Wiped out by the safety car

choices.label: Box for fresh tyres
choices.sub: Grip for the restart, hand over track position

choices.label: Stay out and defend
choices.sub: Keep the lead on tyres that are done

outcomes.box: New rubber under a safety car is close to free, and it only works if the cars behind stay out. If they all follow you in, you have spent your lead for nothing.
outcomes.stay: You keep the lead and you restart on tyres with nothing left, with a queue of fresher cars in your mirrors and no gap to hide in.

cards.reveal: Leclerc came in. At the flag it was P1 Leclerc, P2 Russell, P3 Hamilton.

cards.title: Every gap on track, erased
cards.text: Leclerc was leading when it came out and stayed out. Neutralised until lap 51. Every gap on track was wiped, so a lead built over twenty laps was worth nothing at the restart, and whoever had fresher tyres underneath him suddenly had a race again.

cards.title: Leclerc wins it
cards.text: P1 Leclerc · P2 Russell · P3 Hamilton. After 52 laps and the best part of two hours, Russell crossed the line 0.427s behind, which is less than the time it takes to read this sentence. The gaps at the end of a race almost never reflect the gaps during it.

cards.title: How far behind was Russell at the flag?
cards.text: 52 laps, the best part of two hours of racing, and the whole thing comes down to this one number.
cards.reveal: 0.427 seconds after 52 laps. A single trip down the pit lane costs about 30s today, which is 69 times the margin this race was decided by.
